questions.question: An LP has equality and $\ge$ constraints, so no slack basis gives a feasible start. In the two-phase method, what is the purpose of Phase I?
options: To find the optimal solution of the original objective
To find a feasible basis for the original constraints
To remove the surplus variables from the constraints
To show that the original objective is bounded above

questions.question: In the two-phase method, artificial variables $R_1,\dots,R_k\ge0$ are added to the equality and $\ge$ rows. Which objective does Phase I optimize?
options: Maximize $\sum_iR_i$, the total of the artificials
Maximize the original objective with each $R_i$ kept
Maximize $r=-\sum_iR_i$, i.e. make the artificials small
Maximize $-\sum_iS_i$, the negative sum of the surpluses

questions.question: In the two-phase method, Phase I maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$ over the augmented constraints with artificial variables $R_i\ge0$. Phase I stops at an optimal value $r^*=-2$. What does this mean for the original LP?
options: No point satisfies its constraints; Phase II is skipped
It is feasible, but Phase II must start from this basis
Its objective can increase without any bound in Phase II
Phase I must continue until $r^*$ is positive

questions.question: In the two-phase method, Phase I maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$ over the augmented constraints with artificial variables $R_i\ge0$. Why can the Phase I objective value never exceed $0$?
options: The simplex method stops as soon as $r=0$
Every $R_i\ge0$, so $-\sum_iR_i\le0$
The original objective is at most $0$
The surplus variables keep $r$ below $0$

questions.question: The constraint $2x_1+x_2\ge4$ is written as $2x_1+x_2-S_1=4$ with surplus $S_1\ge0$. Why is an artificial variable still added to this row for Phase I?
options: Surplus variables cannot appear in any basis
The artificial variable records the excess of $2x_1+x_2$ over $4$
Every constraint row gets an artificial variable
With $x_1=x_2=0$ the row gives $S_1=-4$, not feasible

questions.question: An LP has constraints $x_1+2x_2\ge4$ and $x_1+x_2\le5$, with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which equations, with surplus $S_1$, slack $s_2$ and artificial $R_1$, are used in Phase I?
Phase I for $x_1+2x_2-S_1+R_1=4$, $x_1+x_2+s_2=5$ maximizes $r=-R_1$ and starts with $R_1$ and $s_2$ basic. What are the initial basic values and the initial $r$?
Phase I for $x_1+2x_2-S_1+R_1=4$, $x_1+x_2+s_2=5$ maximizes $r=-R_1$, with $R_1,s_2$ basic. Which objective row, in the form $r+\sum_jq_jx_j=r_0$, is canonical for this basis?
An LP has two equality constraints, one $\ge$ constraint and two $\le$ constraints, all with nonnegative right-hand sides. How many artificial variables does the standard Phase I set-up need?
Phase I uses $x_1+2x_2-S_1+R_1=4$ and $3x_1+x_2+R_2=6$ and maximizes $r=-R_1-R_2$. What is $r$ at the point $x_1=x_2=1$ with $S_1=0$?
Phase I of the two-phase method ends with $r^*=0$ and no artificial variable in the basis. What must be done before Phase II applies simplex?
options: Restart from the slack basis with the original objective row
Keep the Phase I row, since its optimum already solved the LP
Restore the objective, drop artificials, and make the row canonical
Restore the objective and drop artificials; signs read off directly

questions.question: In the two-phase method, why must every artificial variable equal $0$ at a point used as a feasible solution of the original LP?
options: Only then do the augmented rows reduce to the original constraints
Artificial variables are negative at every point of the original LP
Nonzero artificials would make the original objective unbounded
Artificial variables measure the surplus, which must be zero

questions.question: Phase I ends with $r^*=0$, but the artificial variable $R_2$ is still basic with value $0$. Which statement about how to continue is correct?
options: The LP is feasible; first move $R_2$ out of the basis, then drop it
The LP has no feasible solution, because an artificial remains basic
Delete the column of $R_2$ at once and start Phase II
Continue Phase I until $r^*$ becomes strictly positive

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+x_2$ with $x_1+x_2+s_1=6$ and $x_1+2x_2=8$, Phase I ends with basic $s_1=2$, $x_2=4$; the second row reads $\frac{1}{2}x_1+x_2=4$ after the artificial is dropped. Which canonical objective row starts Phase II?
For $\max\ 2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1+2x_2=8$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, Phase I has found the feasible start $(0,4)$ with $z=4$. What optimal value does Phase II reach?

Phase I for $x_1+x_2+s_1=5$ and $2x_1+x_2-S_2+R_2=4$ maximizes $r=-R_2$ from the basis $s_1,R_2$, with canonical row $r-2x_1-x_2+S_2=-4$. Using the most negative coefficient and the smallest ratio, where does Phase I end?

In the two-phase method, Phase I maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$ over the augmented constraints with artificial variables $R_i\ge0$. Which statement correctly links the Phase I optimum $r^*$ to the original constraints?
options: $r^*=0$ guarantees a solution, but solvable systems may give $r^*<0$
Solvable systems give $r^*=0$, but $r^*=0$ may not yield a solution
$r^*=0$ holds only if the original LP has a finite optimum
$r^*=0$ holds exactly when the original constraints have a solution

questions.question: Phase I of the two-phase method maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$ after every row has been given a nonnegative right-hand side. Which outcomes can Phase I itself have?
options: A finite optimum, or an unbounded $r$ when the LP is large
A finite optimum, or no feasible start for Phase I itself
Always a finite optimum $r^*\le0$, never an unbounded $r$
Always the optimum $r^*=0$, since artificials can be removed

questions.question: An LP contains the equality constraint $x_1-x_2=-3$ with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which row should be used for it in the Phase I set-up, with artificial $R_1\ge0$?

An LP has constraints $x_1+x_2\ge4$, $x_1\le1$, $x_2\le2$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Phase I uses $x_1+x_2-S_1+R_1=4$ plus slacks for the other rows and maximizes $r=-R_1$. What is the Phase I optimal value $r^*$?
